Fixes #794

## What changed

`apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx` (the `/` palette's Enter at line 837, the send at line 844), `Sidebar.tsx:165` (rename field) and `PromptDialog.tsx:110` (dialog accept) each read `event.key === "Enter"` and acted on it. While an IME candidate is open that Enter belongs to the IME: the composer sent the draft with the pinyin still in it (`蛋白` instead of the `蛋白质` still being chosen), the palette could select a skill, and the two single-line fields could commit.

The four listeners now share one pure rule, `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts`:

- `commitsOnEnter(event)` is false unless `key === "Enter"`;
- false while `nativeEvent.isComposing` or a top-level `isComposing` is true — React keeps the flag on the native event, a bare KeyboardEvent has it on itself;
- false for `keyCode === 229`, the form some IMEs (notably on Windows) report for the confirming Enter without setting any composition flag;
- true otherwise, so the Enter after the candidate is accepted still sends and accepts as before.

Shift+Enter stays at the call site, because it differs there: the composer still requires `!shiftKey` before it sends, while the single-line rename and dialog fields have no newline to give it to. Nothing else in the four listeners changed; no devDependency was added, and no DOM is needed because the rule is a pure function.

# fail 6

The six failures are exactly the composition paths: composer send, palette selection, sidebar rename, dialog accept, the native-event-only shape, and keyCode 229. 810.author: HugoXK
810.body:
Fixes #809

## What changed

Two files, and the split matters for review: `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` **+99/−3** is the whole production change (one linear scan in `protectBigIntegers`, the token map, and the restore calls on the three render paths), while `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts` **+329/−0** is new tests only — no production code there. `JSON.parse` rounds every integer beyond 2^53, so a stored 64-bit id previewed with different digits than the document holds. The preview now keeps the stored literal:

- `protectBigIntegers` walks the document once, copies strings verbatim, and replaces only integer tokens that `JSON.parse` cannot represent (`!Number.isSafeInteger`) with placeholders before parsing.
- Each placeholder is minted per document: `createBigIntegerMarker()` returns a fresh random uuid prefix (U+0001 … U+0002), a counter keeps the placeholders within one document distinct, and the controls cannot appear in a JSON string without an escape, so text a user wrote can never be a placeholder.
- `restoreBigIntegers` puts the digits back through an exact token→literal map on the three render paths: table cells, `rawJson.source`, and the `json-source` view. The quoted shape written by `JSON.stringify` is restored first, so the digits come back as a JSON **number**, not as a string holding the digits; the bare shape used by table cells comes second. A safe number keeps its exact old rendering, and a string that merely looks like a big number is never touched.

No new dependency, no change to `packages/artifact-manager`, jobs, CAS or storage; the #805 BOM strip is untouched.

The earlier tip `b397911b` is superseded: it restored only the bare placeholder, so the raw and source views emitted `"sample_id": "9007199254740993"` (a string where the document holds a number) and its fixed `sd-bigint:` prefix could be forged by document text. This tip fixes both.

## Ran

- Red, on the branch parent `8708320f` plus the test commit only: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → `# tests 52 / # pass 47 / # fail 5`; failures `not ok 48 - json preview keeps big integers as numbers in the raw and source views`, `49 - json preview leaves user text that spells an old placeholder untouched`, `50 - json preview round-trips a big integer document through JSON.parse`, `51 - big integer placeholders are generated per document and are not the old prefix`, `52 - json preview keeps placeholders for many big integers apart`. The original case still failed the same way (`not ok 46`, cell `9007199254740992` vs `9007199254740993`).
- Green, on this tip `7ac867dc`: same command → `# tests 52 / # pass 52 / # fail 0`.
- The new block covers, text-level and type-level:
  - record array `[{"sample_id":9007199254740993,"label":"x"}]` → `dataset-table`; the cell is `9007199254740993`, `rawJson.source` matches `"sample_id": 9007199254740993` with the digit string `9007199254740993`, and never contains `"9007199254740993"`.
  - `{"run_id":12345678901234567890}` → `json-source`, `parsed: true`, matches `"run_id": 12345678901234567890`.
  - a bare scalar `9007199254740993` → source is exactly `9007199254740993`; `[9007199254740993]` → `[\n  9007199254740993\n]`, digits taken from the text, not from a rounded parse.
  - `JSON.parse(rawJson.source)` / `JSON.parse(source)` deep-equal the stored document's `JSON.parse` (structure is not disturbed by the placeholders), alongside the digit-string assertions above.
  - document text that spells the retired `sd-bigint:` sentinel survives character for character, with and without a real big integer in the same document; a token shape the call never minted also survives.
  - `createBigIntegerMarker()` returns a different value per call, carries the U+0001 prefix, and does not start with the retired `sd-bigint:`.
  - 12 distinct big integers in one document keep their own digits (placeholders whose counters share a prefix never eat each other).
  - regression: `42` stays `"42"`, a `"9007199254740993"` string stays a string, a nested object still renders as `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)`.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` on this tip → `# tests 1784 / # pass 1779 / # fail 5`. All five are the known environment gaps, none in the preview code: `not ok 785` (real uvicorn research run), `not ok 966`, `968`, `1346` (PDF extraction, needs reportlab), `not ok 1523` (nested-userns Codex runner).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` → exit 0.
- Single file probe: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts`.

## Not run

- L2/L3 E2E layers, `services/gateway` and `packages/*` suites, real browser UI: the change is confined to preview rendering and covered by the UT above.

## Impact

- Artifacts that store 64-bit identifiers (`sample_id`, `run_id`, timestamps in nanoseconds) now preview with the digits they hold, in the table cell, the raw JSON view and the JSON source view — and the raw/source views keep them as JSON numbers.
- Safe numbers, strings and nested values render exactly as before; CSV/TSV parsing and job shapes are untouched.
- No public API, schema or stored-format change.

814.author: ink999107
814.body:
## Problem

Evolve is the one capability that keeps running and producing results after the turn that started it ends, but the desktop app had no way to reach it: `/evolve-design` opened nothing, so a search could only be designed, confirmed and watched in the web client. A user working in the desktop app has to switch surfaces mid-task, and the run they left behind is unreachable from where they are.

## What this adds

- **Create dialog** — collects the two things a person actually knows (what should get better, which search algorithm fits) and hands that sentence to the conversation as the command the user would have typed. The agent still designs the scorecard, runs the probe and owns the checkpoints.
- **Checkpoint pace switch** — on by default. Turning it off sends `/evolve-design --no-confirm`: the agent still does the work of every step and still reports each checkpoint, labelled as automatic, but does not wait for a reply between them. Checkpoint 3's cost summary is kept, and a blocker that needs a decision (missing dataset, ambiguous goal, an approval the agent cannot give) still stops. The pace is recorded on the goal as `checkpointMode`; an absent field reads as `confirm`, which is what every existing run did.
- **Checkpoint cards** — each of the four checkpoints is drawn as a card in the transcript rather than as more prose: the step (`检查点 1/4`), the question, the few lines to read, and two answers — confirm and continue, or write the change in the card and send it from there. Once a later turn exists the card folds to its header, so a finished design reads as four lines instead of four screens; the card still waiting on you stays open. A run with the pace switch off still shows the card, marked automatic, with no buttons. The card is read from the answer's own `evolve-checkpoint` fence (a block tagged with the skill's name, `evolve-design`, is read the same way), so it survives a reload; a client that does not draw cards falls back to the block as readable code.
- **Session shelf** — a thin row under the session header. A running search stays reachable when the panel is closed, and a session that never used evolve renders exactly as before.
- **Result panel** — follows the run's SSE stream, falls back to polling the run list, and answers in order: best score and how it moved, the candidate table, a selected candidate's diff, and why it was rejected. The inspector becomes a drawer on a narrow window.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop`: `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` — 760 pass, including new command parsing, dialog, shelf, panel, pace-switch, checkpoint-fence and checkpoint-card cases.
- `services/api` evolution suites (proposal, pre-flight, call budget, thinking control) — 51/51.
- `packages/evolve` 11/11, `packages/schema` 29/29.
- The desktop e2e suite gains `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` with a mocked evolve runtime, including three checkpoint-card journeys: confirm sends the reply, an automatic card asks for nothing, and a change is written and sent from inside the card (the composer is never touched). Playwright is not installed in this worktree, so it runs in CI rather than locally.

## Acceptance

The end-to-end path is the tutorial sample in `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`), and the UI review tracked in #798 is the other acceptance item.

Related to #798 — this PR does not close it.

830.author: HugoXK
830.body:
Fixes #829

## What this fixes

`parseDelimitedTable` returned `columns: lines[0]` next to `rows: lines.slice(1, maxRows + 1)`, while `ScientificArtifacts.tsx` prints one `<th>` per column and one `<td>` per cell with no padding and no truncation on either side (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:248` and `:249`). One ragged line sheared the whole grid: an extra cell landed under no header, a short row left the tail cells empty. A 400 KB file holding one 200,000-field line then asked for `100 × 200,001` cells and a 60.8 MB response.

The preview is now a rectangle, bounded by two server-side constants, and everything it leaves out is reported instead of silently dropped.

## The rule at this tip (`0477d328`)

- **Width**: `width = min(widest line of the whole file, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`. Every returned row is padded or sliced to that width; header names come first and in order, and columns past the header are named `""`.
- **`MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001`**: a 1,000-column matrix plus the row-label column, which is also the widest legitimate table header this repository exercises. A 1,002-column table is therefore clipped to 1,001 and the payload says so: `clippedColumns: {total: 1002, shown: 1001}`.
- **`MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS = 100`**, and the request parameter is `Math.min(MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS, parsePositiveInt(maxRowsParam, …))` — a client can lower the height, never raise it.
- **The payload bound is those two constants**: `100 × 1,001 = 100,100` cells, independent of the file's size and of `?maxRows=`. Measured worst case at this tip is 308,291 B ≈ 0.294 MiB, against 60,801,272 B for the shape above.
- **No division by a row count anywhere.** The column set is a property of the file, so the same file returns the same columns at `maxRows=1` and at `maxRows=1000`. Two earlier attempts divided the cell budget by the requested rows, which made the grid's shape a function of the request — `#829`'s square/sheared fork.
- **Clipping is reported, not silent**: the payload carries `clippedColumns: {total, shown}`, `clippedCells = Σ over returned rows max(0, row.length − width)`, and `warnings: string[]` (`[]` when the preview is whole). Cells lost to the header's own clipping go into `clippedColumns`, not into `clippedCells`. The viewer renders both signals, each conditionally (`> 0` only), in en and zhCN (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:246-254`).
- **The JSON record-array path** (`recordArrayTable`) is untouched apart from reporting `clippedCells: 0`, `clippedColumns: {total: n, shown: n}`, `warnings: []`; `totalRows` and `truncated` behave exactly as before.

Forbidden: keeping a ragged fallback behind a `ragged` flag. It leaves the shear in place for exactly the wide tables this PR claims to fix, and keeps the row shape dependent on `maxRows`.

## Measured at this tip

| case | columns | shown | cells | bytes | `clippedColumns` | `clippedCells` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200,001-column header, 600 short rows (default) | 200,001 | 1,001 | 100,100 | 308,291 | `{200001, 1001}` | 0 |
| same, `maxRows=500` (clamped to 100) | 200,001 | 1,001 | 100,100 | 308,291 | `{200001, 1001}` | 0 |
| wide row outside the window, `maxRows=1` | 200,001 | 1,001 | 1,001 | 6,704 | `{200001, 1001}` | 0 |
| same, `maxRows=1000` (clamped to 100) | 200,001 | 1,001 | 100,100 | 305,454 | `{200001, 1001}` | 199,000 |
| 100 named columns, 2 rows | 100 | 100 | 200 | 2,395 | `{100, 100}` | 0 |
| 200 named columns, 2 rows | 200 | 200 | 400 | 4,495 | `{200, 200}` | 0 |
| 20,000 rows × 6 cells (first row 1 cell) | 6 | 6 | 600 | 3,335 | `{6, 6}` | 0 |
| pathological: 2-column header, 100 rows, one 200,001-cell line | 200,001 | 1,001 | 100,100 | 305,455 | `{200001, 1001}` | 199,000 |

The last two rows are the two must-fixes from review: a long file keeps its sixth column (`6`, not `floor(100000/20000) = 5`), and the pathological line is bounded at 305,455 B instead of 60,801,272 B. Rows 1 and 3/4 are the same file at different `maxRows`: the column set is identical.

## Behaviour changes to state plainly

- **Known limitation**: a two-column header meeting one line wider than `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` is rendered at 1,001 columns, so 999 of them carry empty header names. The values are honest and the width is capped, so nothing is wrong on screen, but the table is wider than the file's header suggests — the surplus-column presentation is a separate design question, tracked in `#839`.
- **API contract**: `maxRows` larger than 100 now returns 100 rows. Before, `?maxRows=1000` returned 1,000 rows; `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS = 100` is what makes the payload bound a constant rather than a function of the request. No caller in this repository asks for more than 100 (`apps/web/src/api/artifacts.ts` only forwards an optional value; the `apps/desktop` reader is local CSV and does not use this endpoint), so there is no in-repo regression — but an out-of-repo caller asking for more than 100 gets 100.
- **One assertion inside this PR changes conclusion**: `a row past maxRows must not add a column` was added by this PR itself in `ff2046aa`, and the square grid requires the opposite conclusion (a wide line outside the window still sets the width). The 1,001-column "keep a wide header whole" case is also this PR's own (`72ab2803`). Neither exists on base `865102a3` or on `upstream/main` — the base has no `clippedCells` and no cap — so no upstream contract is being rewritten.

## What changed

Five files, `+386/−9` against `865102a3`:

| file | change | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` | +97/−6 | the two constants, the width rule, pad/slice, `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells`/`warnings` |
| `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts` | +267/−0 | tests only |
| `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx` | +12/−3 | viewer shows both clip signals |
| `apps/web/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` | +6/−0 | payload type mirror |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` | +4/−0 | clipped-columns and clipped-cells strings, en and zhCN |

No new dependency, no manifest or lockfile change, no change to `packages/artifact-manager`, jobs or CAS.

## Ran

- **Red before the fix, at the test commit**: `66 tests / 61 pass / 5 fail` — `keeps every row as wide as its columns` (`["a","b"]` where `["a","b",""]` was expected), `a long file keeps its sixth column` (`5 !== 6`), `caps a pathological line` (`1000 !== 1001`), `keeps a wide header whole` (`200001`), `same columns whatever maxRows` (2 vs 1000 columns).
- **Green at this tip `0477d32825bd7114f550e36757747ff9bbb5c731`**: `66 / 66 / 0`, run with the three commands below.
- Gate commands, verbatim, each `exit 0` at this tip:
  - `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → 0
  - `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → 0
  - `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` → 0 (`66` tests, `66` pass, `0` fail)
- One earlier tip failed CI on `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` only, because a new test read `many.rows` before narrowing the union; the fix was a `assert.fail` narrow, no assertion was relaxed and no case was deleted.
- `#650`'s quoted-delimiter case, `#654`'s BOM case and the "a row past `maxRows` must not add a column" case are all in `dashboard.test.ts` and green.
- GitHub Actions at this tip: `completed / success`; `merge-gate` green. `CodeCheck (GitCode)` shows red on the mirror for this SHA and its detail page is not readable from here (a JS shell with no API); it is not a required check — the ruleset requires `merge-gate` only.

## Labels

If the token cannot apply a `release:*` label, a maintainer needs to add exactly one (the previous PR hit a 403 there).

| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/RunnerResources.tsx:589` | `event.key !== "Enter"` | asked for the key-file listing a second time (2 requests for one Enter) |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/Timeouts.tsx:159` | `event.key !== "Enter"` | committed the timeout field without blurring first |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:200` | `event.key === "Enter"` | picked the highlighted model while the candidate was open (`''` → `'gpt-4o-mini'`) |

All six now call `commitsOnEnter(event)`; the predicates read exactly one rule and no site keeps its own copy. Shift handling stays at each call site where it differs (`App.tsx:5052` keeps `event.shiftKey` first, as the composer already did).

`apps/web` and `apps/desktop` each keep their own copy of the rule (`apps/web/src/ime-enter.ts:36`, `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts:36`). They are byte-identical, and each app has the same group of rule tests. The web app cannot import from `apps/desktop`, and the rule is 12 lines, so a shared package or a `@sciencediscvery/schema` entry would be more coupling than the duplication costs. **When a third consumer appears, this becomes a shared package.**

Five other `key === "Enter"` sites are deliberately untouched, because they are activation, not submission — each one also handles Space and sends or commits no field: `apps/desktop/src/views/ToolIoBlock.tsx:69`, `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:528`, `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ListSelect.tsx:167`, `apps/web/src/IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx:287`, `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphView.tsx:155`.

### Test support

The desktop app has no DOM test environment, so the three desktop sites are driven through `apps/desktop/tests/support/dom-renderer.ts`, which re-exports `act` and `create` from `react-test-renderer` — the same renderer `apps/web` already uses. That adds a real devDependency to the desktop app rather than reaching into the web app's `node_modules`:

- `apps/desktop/package.json`: `"react-test-renderer": "19.2.7"`. `apps/web/package.json:56` already declares the same version in its own `devDependencies`, so this follows the repository's existing shape — each app declares the test renderer its own tests import — instead of introducing a dependency. The two apps are separate workspace packages, so `apps/desktop` cannot resolve a dependency only `apps/web` declares, and reaching into `apps/web/node_modules` would tie the desktop suite to the web app's install.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: three lines in the `apps/desktop` importer's `devDependencies` only (`packages`/`snapshots` unchanged — the version was already resolved for `apps/web`). This was edited by hand, not by `pnpm install`: a plain `pnpm install` on this branch also upgrades `@types/d3-selection`, `@types/d3-zoom` and `@types/ssh2`, which does not belong in this change. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only` exits 0 on the result: the lockfile already agrees with both `package.json` files, so the frozen install CI runs resolves the same tree and never rewrites it. Its only side effect here is dropping the file's UTF-8 BOM, so the commit keeps the BOM.
- `apps/desktop/tests/support/react-test-renderer.d.ts`: the package ships no types and the desktop `tsconfig` includes `tests/**`, so it needs a local declaration.

`App.tsx` is the session shell: mounting it needs a live session client, the router and the async bootstrap that creates the run before the header exists, so a component test would spend its assertions on the mount machinery and would be one fixture away from testing something other than the guard under change. Its test therefore pins the source line, the approach this repository already takes in `apps/web/tests/artifactTree.test.tsx:234`, `:248`, `:300` and `apps/web/tests/ArtifactLifecycleControls.test.tsx:148`. The pin asserts the guard's exact shape, so an edit that drops the rule fails the test instead of regressing silently.

## Validation

Branch shape: `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c` (upstream `main`) → `760c810d0ae157376cb918c5349a99ef770ae6f9` (tests only, red) → `a876b947b40df1dfd1757b6006db9655d0b93d6b` (fix, this tip).

```

apps/desktop  # tests 718   # pass 715   # fail 3

The desktop failures are the three user-visible ones: `expected: 1 actual: 2` (a second `/api/remote-hosts/key-files` request), `expected: false actual: true` (the field blurred and committed), `expected: '' actual: 'gpt-4o-mini'` (the model was picked by the Enter that belonged to the IME). The web failures include the key-file browser browsing `+ [ "~/.ssh" ]` where `[]` was expected, the `keyCode: 229` rename that still blurred, and the two `App.tsx` pins. The control cases (composition ended, Shift+Enter left to the caller, non-Enter keys) pass on both sides.

Green at this tip:

```

apps/desktop  # tests 718   # pass 718   # fail 0

- `cd apps/web && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 1199 tests, 1199 pass, 0 fail.
- `cd apps/desktop && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 718 tests, 718 pass, 0 fail (712 on this branch's base; the new file adds 6).

- `git grep -n 'key === "Enter"\|key !== "Enter"' -- apps/web/src apps/desktop/src` → 7 hits: the two rule bodies and the five activation sites above. No listener keeps its own submission predicate.
- `git grep -n 'nativeEvent.isComposing' -- apps/web/src apps/desktop/src` → no hit; both half-guards now go through the rule.

One note for reproducing the desktop numbers: a working copy whose `apps/desktop/node_modules` predates this devDependency fails the new file with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: react-test-renderer` — that is the install, not the code. After `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (what CI does) the suite is 718 on a fresh clone with no extra linking. Linking the renderer in from a *different* pnpm store produces a duplicate-React `TypeError` instead, so the numbers above were measured with every package resolved from one store.

[Bug]: Anthropic Messages UI errors report OpenAI stream and unsupported reasoning_split

Fixes #822

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## Review answers — F1 on `385e48a2`

**F1 (high, must-fix): a Swarm-side constant overrode the run's configured thinking mode.** Fixed on this tip `99491977c7d04bf0ad235e8dbfabad0aa2a130b0`; the run's own choice now decides, and the flag only decides while that choice is open.

The translation now runs through one expression, in the order the review prescribed:

```ts
const thinkingMode = body.thinking ? body.thinking.type as "enabled" | "disabled"
  : endpoint.thinkingMode === undefined || endpoint.thinkingMode === "auto"
    ? (typeof body.reasoning_split === "boolean" ? (body.reasoning_split ? "enabled" : "disabled") : undefined)
    : undefined;
requestEndpoint = { ...endpoint, ...(thinkingMode ? { thinkingMode } : {}) };
```

- `body.thinking` (the request's own control) still wins outright.
- An endpoint that already carries `enabled` or `disabled` — the conversation-level choice the run started with — is left untouched, so `reasoning_split: true` can no longer turn thinking back on behind a user who switched it off.
- Only `auto` (or no mode at all) is the flag's to decide.

On the review's test sentence, which asks that `auto` also stay unchanged: `auto` is not a mode that can be "turned on", and the flag deciding it is the review's own fix expression. Measured through `createModelRequest` (MiniMax-M3, `anthropic-messages`) the three modes serialize as:

| endpoint `thinkingMode` | serialized request |
|---|---|
| `auto` | no thinking field at all — the provider default |
| `enabled` | `thinking: {"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"}` + `output_config: {"effort":"high"}` |
| `disabled` | `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` |

So the case that mattered — a run started with thinking **off** silently getting the adaptive control — is now closed, and `auto` is pinned by its own test as flag-decided, which is what the fix expression does.

Tests added by this round:

- `a run's own thinking mode wins over the Swarm reasoning_split flag` — `disabled` with `reasoning_split: true` stays `disabled`, `enabled` with `reasoning_split: false` stays `enabled`.
- `an auto thinking mode lets the Swarm reasoning_split flag decide` — `auto` and `undefined`, both flag values, each resolving to the flag's mode.

## What changed

The model gateway now accepts Swarm's `reasoning_split` and translates it into the endpoint's thinking mode. It is a transport flag, not a provider field, so it never travels further:

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:274` — `reasoning_split` joins the accepted inbound fields, so it is no longer refused as unknown.
- `:293-297` — the flag becomes the endpoint's `thinkingMode` (`true` → `enabled`, `false` → `disabled`) **only when the run has no explicit mode**; `body.thinking` and an endpoint already set to `enabled`/`disabled` both win over it.
- `:84-85` — the field is declared on `ChatRequest`, so the gateway says what it accepts.

Nothing else moves. `toModelRequest` (`:113-125`) builds `{ history, systemPrompt, tools }` field by field rather than spreading the body, so the flag cannot reach the provider request; the new tests assert both halves (endpoint carries `thinkingMode`, serialized endpoint carries no `reasoning_split`) and that a parameter the gateway genuinely cannot honour (`frequency_penalty`) is still a 400.

### Why the run failed before any provider call

| Evidence | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:275` throws `Unsupported gateway parameters: …` inside the admission `try`, and `:255` `fail(400, …)` writes `{"error":{"message":…,"type":"model_gateway_error"}}` | the `400` and the `type` in the report are produced by this repository's loopback gateway, not by the provider |
| the upstream-error path (`Model request failed with status …`, `packages/model/src/client.ts:576`) adds a prefix the reported text does not have | the request never left the gateway, so nothing was sent to Anthropic or to MiniMax and then refused |
| `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:38` — "The model, as JiuwenSwarm sees it: an OpenAI chat-completions endpoint on loopback" | the inbound hop is chat-completions even when the run's endpoint is Anthropic Messages, which is why a chat-completions-only flag can arrive on an Anthropic run at all |

So the report is one failure with two confusing labels: a chat-completions flag arriving on the inbound hop, refused by a whitelist that was written before Swarm started sending it.

### Why `reasoning_split` is there

In this repository the token only exists in `packages/model/src/client.ts:731` (`chatThinkingFields`, `variant === "minimax"`) — an **outbound** field the model client writes for a MiniMax model. The one the gateway refused arrived **inbound** in Swarm's body, which sets the same flag for a MiniMax model. The Anthropic path never writes it (`toAnthropicMessages`/`anthropicThinkingFields` carry no such field), so it should never have been able to fail an Anthropic Messages run.

### What this does not change

The outer wording, `openAI API async stream error: BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {…}`, belongs to JiuwenSwarm's own OpenAI client, an external package; this repository has no such literal (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/events.py` only forwards `run.failed`'s reason). This PR makes the run stop failing on the flag. Renaming that outer line is an adapter/upstream change and is out of scope here.

## Validation

Before the first fix, the same request against the gateway returns `400 Unsupported gateway parameters: reasoning_split`; after it, `200`, and the endpoint still resolves to `anthropic-messages` rather than falling back to chat-completions.

Commits, in order: `5caedeaf` (test: accept the flag) → `385e48a2` (fix) → `a3103cac` (test: the run's mode wins) → `99491977` (fix, this tip).

Red at the first tests-only commit `5caedeaf54f05654d817679fc13f1c13d75f5db7`, where the whitelist is still unchanged:

```
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts   # tests 53  # pass 52  # fail 1
not ok 53 - a MiniMax reasoning_split transport flag from Swarm is honoured, not rejected as an unknown parameter
```

Red at the second tests-only commit `a3103cac13a66342860c123611848105110f35b9`, where the precedence is still the wrong way round:

```
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts   # tests 55  # pass 54  # fail 1
not ok 54 - a run's own thinking mode wins over the Swarm reasoning_split flag
  error: thinkingMode:"disabled" plus reasoning_split:true must keep the run's choice: 'enabled' !== 'disabled'
```

Green at this tip `99491977c7d04bf0ad235e8dbfabad0aa2a130b0`:

```
services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts   # tests 55  # pass 55  # fail 0
```

## Ran

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts`: 55 tests, 55 pass, 0 fail at this tip; 54 pass, 1 fail at the precedence red commit; 52 pass, 1 fail at the first tests-only commit.
- `typecheck`: exit 0.
- A local probe of the reported shape: an Anthropic endpoint plus `reasoning_split: true` went from `400 Unsupported gateway parameters` to `200`, with the endpoint still `anthropic-messages`.
- The precedence probe: `{ thinkingMode: "disabled" }` plus `reasoning_split: true` now keeps `disabled` and serializes `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}`; before the fix the same input produced `enabled` and the adaptive control.
- `git grep -n 'reasoning_split' -- services packages apps` → the field is accepted and translated in the gateway, written for MiniMax only in `packages/model/src/client.ts:731`, and nowhere serialized to a provider.

## Not run

- No live call to a real Anthropic or MiniMax endpoint: the gateway is exercised against the repository's fake streamer, which is what pins the failure (the request never left the gateway in the first place).
- No UI journey: the user-visible change is that the run no longer fails with this 400 and no longer overrides the run's thinking mode; the surface that renders the error is unchanged.

## Labels

If the token cannot apply a `release:*` label, a maintainer needs to add exactly one (the previous PR hit a 403 there).

Fixes #828

## Review answers — four threads raised on `a3b1e688`

All four are fixed on this tip `6c8b09f3f274f928ecfed4dbbeb6adc75081da0e`, one red-first commit pair each, same branch, same base `865102a3` (no rebase).

**F2 — an `in` guard walked the prototype chain, so a header named after an inherited member showed a value the file never had.** `readCell` / `writeCell` now use own-property semantics everywhere: padding is checked with `Object.hasOwn(row, field)`, reads go through `Object.hasOwn(row, field) ? row[field] : undefined`, and writes go through one helper — `__proto__` is defined with `Object.defineProperty` (the inherited setter would otherwise drop the value), everything else is a plain assignment so the million-row path is not slowed. `a,toString\n1\n` now yields an empty `toString` column with `missingCount 1`; `a,__proto__\n1,2\n` yields an own key with an empty value — Papa itself loses that assignment, so empty is the honest answer rather than a fabricated `[object Object]`.

**F4 — a duplicate header was shown and exported as Papa's `a_1`.** The `step` callback now captures `result.meta.renamedHeaders` (typed locally as `Papa.ParseMeta & { renamedHeaders?: Record<string, string> | null }`, no dependency change), `ColumnProfile` gained an optional `header`, and `columnHeaderName` is `column.header ?? column.id`. The grid and the export therefore show the name the file wrote, while the id stays the unique key. A new warning `csv.importRenamedColumns` (en + zhCN) says the rename happened. A test also pins `a,a,a_1\n1,2,3\n`, where Papa's ids are `a`, `a_2`, `a_1`: the column genuinely called `a_1` keeps its own name and the export reads `a,a,a_1`, so the mapping is keyed by renamed id and does not touch a column that was already unique.

**F5 — a header column named `__rowId` was overwritten by the generated row id.** It is now excluded from the header fields (the base behaviour: the column is not rendered) **and reported**: `csv.importReservedColumn` (en + zhCN) names `__rowId` to the reader. Rationale, stated rather than implied: the internal row id and a user column name share one namespace, and renaming the internal key would touch the grid, the filters and the selection; hiding-with-a-warning is the smaller change and no longer silent. `a,__rowId\n1,2\n` yields the column `a`, a row id of `row-2`, and that warning.

**F6 — the surplus-fold warning was off by one.** The code keeps `kept - 1` single-cell surplus columns and folds the rest into the last one, so the message was rewritten rather than given `kept - 1` (which would read "the first 1 surplus columns" when `kept` is 2): en `…the surplus columns are capped at {kept}, and the cells past the last one are joined into it…`, zh `溢出列最多保留 {kept} 列，超出最后一列的单元格会合并进该列…`. The `A row has {count} cells past the header` prefix is unchanged, so the earlier `497 cells past the header` assertion still holds. A test pins `a,b\n1,2,3,4,5,6\n` → `__extra_1 = 3`, `__extra_2 = "4, 5, 6"`, warning contains `capped at 2` and no longer `first 2`, plus the zh text.

## Review answers — three threads raised on `c4292825`

**F1 (high, must-fix) — padding every row to the widest record was O(rows × max width).** Reproduced before touching it. Fixture: 3-column header, 20,000 ordinary rows, one record with 500 cells — before **12.7 s / 1050 MB heap / 500 columns / 10,020,501 cells**, after **264 ms / 30 MB / 6 columns / 140,007 cells**. (The review measured 5.5 s / 1.2 GB on its own fixture: same cause, same order.) The bound is **surplus columns = `min(16, max(2, header width))`**, so a table materialises at most `2 × header width` cells per row (`3 ×` for a one-column header). **Header columns are not part of the bound** — a legitimate 200-column header still returns 200 columns, one cell per row. Past the bound the trailing surplus cells are joined into the last surplus column, and `table.warnings` gains one entry. Tests: `caps surplus columns so one wide record cannot widen every row` (6 columns, `cells <= rows × 7`, warning) and `keeps a legitimate wide header without folding its columns` (200 columns, `width + 1` keys per row).

**F2 — a real `__parsed_extra` column lost its own value.** Fixed, but not with the array check as suggested, because that check cannot separate the two shapes. papaparse 5.5.4 (`papaparse.js:1303–1311`) routes on the **field name**, not on overflow: `if (field === '__parsed_extra') { row[field] = row[field] || []; row[field].push(value); }`. A header column literally named `__parsed_extra` therefore also arrives as an array — measured: `a,__parsed_extra\n1,x\n` → `fields ["a","__parsed_extra"]`, `data [{"a":"1","__parsed_extra":["x"]}]`. So the discriminator is the header: when it contains that name, the first array element is that column's value and only the remaining ones are surplus; the key is deleted only where the header does not claim it. Tests pin both shapes.

**F3 — column order came from `Object.keys`.** Fixed as suggested: `rectangularizeRows` returns the ordered id list (header in file order, then surplus) and `profileRows` takes it as an optional argument, keeping the key union as the fallback for other callers. Tests: `10,2` → columns `['10','2']`, grid header `["#","10","2"]`, export `10,2`; `2024,2025,2` stays in file order. This one was pre-existing and is folded in because the ordering it breaks is this PR's stated goal.

## What changed

Seven files, `+447/−19` against `865102a3`:

| file | change | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts` | +148/−9 | the fix, the surplus bound, own-property reads, renamed headers |
| `apps/web/tests/CsvArtifact.test.tsx` | +261/−3 | tests only |
| `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/chart-spec/filters.ts` | +26/−4 | `columnHeaderName`, positional `tableToCsv`, `rowsToCsv` deleted |
| `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/types.ts` | +2/−0 | `ColumnProfile.header` |
| `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/components/VirtualDataTable.tsx` | +2/−1 | header cell renders the name |
| `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx` | +2/−2 | export calls the positional helper |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` | +6/−0 | renamed / reserved / surplus warnings, en and zhCN |

`parseCsvText` decided a table's columns from the union of the parsed rows' keys (everything except `__rowId`), while `:222` read the real header `result.meta.fields` only to pass it to `inferTableKind`. Two symptoms followed, and they are the same bug seen from both sides: a row wider than the header made Papa park the surplus cells under `__parsed_extra`, which then became a sortable, typed, exported column named after a library internal; and a header column that no row filled had no key in the union, so it was absent from `columns` altogether.

The table is now built from the header, losslessly:

- Width is the header's own columns plus the bounded surplus columns; the header's names stay first and in the file's order, from `meta.fields`.
- Every record is rebuilt to that width: `__parsed_extra` is removed (except where the header claims the name), missing header cells are set to `undefined` (profiled as `null`), and surplus values are written back by position.
- Surplus columns get synthetic ids `__extra_1`, `__extra_2`, … with `label: ""` — the shape an empty header cell (`a,,c`) already produces today.
- `profileRows` takes an optional ordered column list and an optional map from id to the header the file wrote.

Two supporting changes follow: the header cell renders the name rather than the id (`columnHeaderName`), and the export is positional (`tableToCsv`), because the old helper used each field as both value key and header name — handing it the header text would have read `row[""]`.

`#654`'s BOM handling of real header names is untouched (probe: `"\uFEFFa,b\r\n1,2\r\n"` → columns `["a","b"]`, row `[1,2]`), and the `rowId` de-duplication is untouched.

One visible behaviour change to call out: in the positional shape a header name is a data value, so it goes through the same formula neutralisation as the cells. A legitimate header starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` therefore gets the `'` prefix — `-log2FC,b` exports as `'-log2FC,b`. This is deliberate: Excel reads `-log2FC` as a formula.

## Ran

Branch parent `865102a3`; the suite is **1182 tests** there, measured on that base rather than carried over.

Commits, in order: `a1dd498e` (test) → `c8377594` → `b5521c8e` (test) → `c4292825` → `98579012` (test) → `1d02ef47` → `22ca0d3c` (test) → `55c9181c` → `4ee6fb69` (test) → `a3b1e688` → `1217c0c5` (test) → `34913355` → `c26fc2a6` (test) → `466276ce` → `0043339a` (test) → `3eec6f4c` → `bb089876` (test) → `6c8b09f3` (this tip).

- Red at `a1dd498e`, the first test commit: **1186 tests / 1182 pass / 4 fail** — the four cases that commit adds:

  error: 'internal key became a column id: __parsed_extra'
not ok 204 - pads short rows to the header width so no header column disappears
  expected: ['a','b','c']   actual: ['a','b']
not ok 205 - the data table header hides an unnamed overflow column's internal id
  expected: ['#','a','b','']   actual: ['#','a','b','__parsed_extra']
not ok 206 - exports an unnamed overflow column with an empty header name
  expected: 'a,b,'   actual: 'a,b,__parsed_extra'
```

### Included

- Text parsing and retrieval primitives, including JATS, LaTeX, document levels, trigram/search, and citation helpers.

The in-app feedback path only existed as a proposal: nothing collected what a user saw when something broke, so every report started from "it does not work". This wires the whole chain for the web and desktop front ends: a dialog that captures kind, description, frequency and impact (both required, since a report without them cannot be triaged), a draft/history store, and a receipt code the user can quote.

The report is relayed by a Cloudflare Worker into a private GitHub issue, with KV-backed dedupe, per-IP and per-install rate limits and a daily quota so the endpoint cannot be used as a spam funnel. Payload building, redaction, PII detection and the receipt format live in operational-logging so both apps and the tests share one contract, and the offline screen seeds the dialog with the failure's diagnostics so a "cannot reach the local service" report arrives with boot state, origin and user agent already attached.

/kind feature

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

- `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`: the shared contract — payload building, field validation, redaction, PII detection, contact classification and receipt generation, imported by both clients and the Worker so the wire format cannot drift.
- `packages/feedback-worker`: a Cloudflare Worker that relays a submission into a private GitHub issue (labels `source:in-app`, `kind:<kind>`, `needs-triage`, `contact:<type>`), with KV-backed dedupe keyed by reporter and content, a per-IP hourly limit, a per-install daily limit, a daily issue quota, a CORS allowlist, and a 422 fallback that retries without labels so a repository missing a label does not lose the report.
- `apps/web` and `apps/desktop`: the same dialog (kind, description, frequency, impact — frequency and impact mandatory), a draft and a 50-entry history in `localStorage`, the receipt display, a 我要反馈 entry in the desktop sidebar footer, and an entry on the offline screen that pre-fills the failure's diagnostics.
- i18n in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` and in both desktop dictionaries (`text/zh.ts`, `text/en.ts`).

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Closes #844

**What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**：

- Unit tests: `operational-logging` 12 cases, `feedback-worker` 12 cases (CORS, 16 KiB rejection, invalid JSON and wrong field types, success path, duplicate within the window, per-install 429, daily quota 503, GitHub 5xx surfacing 502 without leaking the token, reporter-scoped dedupe, 422 label fallback), plus 8 + 8 status-code mapping and 7 + 7 store cases in the two clients.

- Behaviour checks: 提交 stays disabled until frequency and impact are chosen, with the reason shown; the same content from the same install returns the original receipt instead of opening a second issue; a full-length description still carries the two mandatory triage lines.

849.author: zhaozhaozz
849.body:
Documentation-only changes still run the full CI profile. Unit tests, system tests, mocked end-to-end tests, coverage, and the jobs that run outside a pull request do not read those files, but `merge-gate` fails if those jobs are skipped or their artifacts are missing. The required check name has to stay `merge-gate`.

## Documentation-only selection

A change is documentation-only only when every changed path is `README.md`, `README_zh.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `LICENSE`, `Third_Party_Open_Source_Software_Notice.txt`, a path under `docs/`, or a path under `.agents/skills/` that ends in `.md`. The skill prefix and the `.md` suffix are case-sensitive. Markdown under the product `skills/` directory does not qualify, and neither does a non-Markdown file under `.agents/skills/`. A rename counts both the old path and the new path. An unreadable, empty, or truncated diff keeps the current profile. Markdown under `skills/`, tests, workflows, packages, services, and other product paths keeps it as well.

`policy` makes this decision for `pull_request`, `push`, and `merge_group`. Pull request diffs use the merge base. Push and merge-group diffs use the event's two commits. `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` keep the requested profile. A called workflow keeps the caller's event name, so the diff skip is turned off when the `profile` input is present, including a caller that is itself a documentation-only push.

## What still runs

For a documentation-only change, `policy` still runs and L1 runs only `pnpm docs:check` (`pnpm docs:lint` and `pnpm docs:links`). UT, ST, `e2e-plan`, mocked E2E, coverage, binary, Docker, `real-merge`, and `real-scheduled` are skipped. On a non-draft pull request, a push, and a merge group, `merge-gate` still runs. It requires `policy` and L1 to succeed, expects those skipped jobs to stay skipped, and does not download or reconcile mocked E2E artifacts. Any other diff keeps today's job selection and gate rules, so a skipped UT, ST, or E2E job still fails the gate. A documentation-only draft still runs the documentation check and still skips the heavy jobs and the gate. Repository rulesets are unchanged.

Fixes #848.

## Validation

- `node --test .ci/docs-only.test.mjs .ci/test-layers.test.mjs .ci/real-scheduling.test.mjs`: 29 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `pnpm ci:selftest` (`node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`): 117 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4, failed 0, skipped 0.

A follow-up commit `91e1e920443778c7722f5af814f5b5e95c121838` adds `.agents/skills/**/*.md` to that allowlist. Targeted policy tests after that commit: 30 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm ci:selftest`: 118 passed, 0 failed.

The new tests evaluate the workflow conditions for a documentation-only pull request, push, and merge group, including real E2E, binary, and Docker on a merge group. They also cover a mixed diff, an unreadable diff, manual dispatch, reusable workflow calls, and the existing gate rule that a normal pull request fails when UT, ST, or E2E is skipped. This pull request changes workflow and CI files, so its own Actions run takes the full profile. The documentation-only skip is covered by those tests, not by this run.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. The change selects CI jobs and does not change a product path a user exercises. Product end-to-end was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for the product. CI skips jobs that a documentation-only diff cannot affect. The required check remains `merge-gate`.
Compatibility and migration: none. No ruleset change.

854.body:
Opening a subagent's detail panel froze the desktop app for three to four seconds on a long run. The whole record was parsed and laid out at once — a closed `<details>` still mounts its children — every tool output went through `react-markdown`, and opening a replayed child re-read the whole roster from the API, though the panel only ever shows one child.

## Render a fold's body on first open

A closed native fold still mounts its subtree, so the panel paid for parsing and laying out tool output, the brief and historical steps that nobody could see. The new `Disclosure` component renders its body when the fold is first opened and keeps it afterwards, so reopening is instant. `open` stays uncontrolled: the browser still owns the open state, which is what lets a running step collapse on its own when it finishes. Running thinking stays open, as before.

## Show tool output as text, not Markdown

Tool input, output and progress are terminal text, not prose. They now render in a `<pre>`; the child's replies and thinking still go through Markdown. This removes the largest Markdown parse in the panel, since tool output is most of a long record's bytes.

## Read one child instead of the roster

`GET /api/sessions/:id/subagents/:sid` returns one child with its steps. The panel uses it when a replayed child is opened; a running child keeps following its own stream. On the server the store clones only that child rather than every child in the session. The roster route remains for callers that list children; the contract table and a contract scenario cover the new route.

## Compare repeated steps by field

`mergeSubagentSteps` used to `JSON.stringify` both copies of every step on every stream tick. `content` can be hundreds of kilobytes, so a step that had not changed was still serialized twice. The comparison is now field by field, with prose compared as the string it is and only the small structured fields going through JSON. The field list is a key set that satisfies `Record<keyof SubagentStep, true>`: a field added to the schema fails the build here instead of being silently ignored. A unit test pins that an unchanged step keeps its identity.

Every state — just opened, task open, timeline open with folded rows, one tool step open, failed step with a stack trace, running vs finished thinking — is captured in Chinese and English at 1440x900 with the default panel and at the 480 px minimum. 857.author: HugoXK
857.body:
Fixes #816

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`SessionStore.writeArray` wrote its temp file and then called a bare `rename`, so a transient Windows sharing violation (an antivirus scanner, a search indexer or a backup agent briefly holding the fresh file) rejected the write, and nothing above contained the rejection.

- `services/api/src/store.ts` — **every** replace in the store now goes through the platform facade's `renameReplace`: the state writer (`writeArray`), the deletion journal finalize (`operation.next.json` → `operation.json`), and both journal staging renames (`stageDeletion`, `rollbackStagedDeletion`). The sharing violation belongs to the target file, not to one writer, so leaving the deletion paths on a bare `rename` would have kept the same failure shape on delete/rollback.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` (new) — one replace policy for every platform: 20 attempts, `50 + 25·attempt` ms backoff. Patience is 19 waits, `19 × 50 ms + 25 ms × (0 + … + 18) = 5,225 ms` (about 5.2 s). A non-transient errno such as `ENOSPC` is thrown immediately.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` — the retried errno set is platform-aware (`transientReplaceCodes()`): Windows retries `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY` because its redirector reports all three for a transient hold; POSIX retries only `EPERM`/`EBUSY`, because an `EACCES` there is a lasting mode/ownership problem and `writeArray` is on the chat run path — retrying it would add 5.2 s to every state write of an already-unwritable store instead of failing at once. `ReplaceFileOptions.transientCodes` allows an override.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` — when the attempts are exhausted the throw is a `FileReplaceError` that keeps the last errno in `code` and the original error in `cause`, names the destination and the attempt count, and now also **copies `errno`/`syscall`/`path`/`dest`** from the last failure. A consumer that classified state-write failures on those fields would otherwise have been silently downgraded; `code`, `cause` and the `FileReplaceError` identity are unchanged, so a caller (or a test) that reads them still works.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` — the run scheduler is started with `void`, so nothing observed its rejection. It now attaches a `catch` that logs `run_scheduler_failed` with the session id and the message.
- `services/api/src/platform/os/index.ts` / `win32.ts` / `types.ts` — the retry moves out of the Windows-only adaptation (which now performs the raw rename) up to the facade, so the durable write behaves the same on every platform.

## Where the exhausted write could kill the process

The caller is **`scheduleSessionRuns` (`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3380`)** — the per-session run drain started from every run-creating request. Its body is `void (async () => { … })()`, and the statement that escapes is the **terminal `await store.updateSessionRunStatus(sessionId, next.id, status, …)` inside the inner `finally` (`:3522`)** (plus the `listSessionRuns` in the outer `finally`): the inner `try/catch` does not cover its own `finally`, so a state write that exhausts the retries propagates out of the `while`, through the outer `finally`, and out of a promise nobody awaits. Node 22 treats that as an unhandled rejection and exits — the reported crash.

With the catch: the rejection is logged, `scheduledSessions` has already released the session, and the run keeps the last status it could persist (`running`), which `recoverSessionRuns` turns into `interrupted` at the next start. Nothing is silently lost and the process survives. The regression test below fails on the pre-fix code with exactly the unhandled rejection, so this is pinned rather than argued.

## Red-first evidence

Test commit `ce393efa` (test only) on base `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`, `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test …`:

- `src/store-deletion.test.ts` → `# tests 7 / # pass 6 / # fail 1`
  ```
  not ok 2 - a transient EPERM on the deletion journal finalize is retried
    error: "EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '…/.trash/<id>/operation.next.json' -> '…/.trash/<id>/operation.json'"
  ```
  (the bare rename on the journal path, found in review, fails exactly like the state writer did)
- `src/runs/index.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 15 / # fail 1`
  ```
  not ok 16 - a state write that fails after retries is contained instead of killing the API
    error: 'Could not replace …/session-runs/<id>.json after 20 attempts (EPERM)'
  ```
  (the rejection escapes the voided scheduler and node:test reports it — the crash shape)
- `src/platform/os/replace.test.ts` does not load at `ce393efa`: `transientReplaceCodes` is the new export the platform split (and its POSIX no-retry assertion) needs.

Green at `8cb37d8aa37dab30853d75dfe5462eb2341b29f5`: the same four files `node --import tsx --test src/platform/os/replace.test.ts src/store-deletion.test.ts src/runs/index.test.ts src/store-replace.test.ts` → `# tests 29 / # pass 29 / # fail 0`.

## Verification

| gate | command | exit | reading |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck (recursive) | `pnpm --recursive typecheck` | 0 | — |
| tests typecheck | `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | 0 | — |
| targeted UT | `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/platform/os/replace.test.ts src/store-deletion.test.ts src/runs/index.test.ts src/store-replace.test.ts` | 0 | `29/29` |
| package UT | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` | 1 | `1873 tests / 1868 pass / 5 fail`, all five environmental and untouched by this diff: `No module named uvicorn` in `services/evolve/.venv` (`idea-tree/research-entry.test.ts`), `No module named 'reportlab'` in `services/paper/.venv` (three PDF tests), and `Cannot find module '@openai/codex-linux-x64/package.json'` (`codex.st.test.ts`) |
| static/architecture | `pnpm architecture:check` | 1 | `98/99`; the single failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` calling `bash .ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which cannot create its temp dir (`/home/xuke/.cache/uv/...: Read-only file system (os error 30)`) on this host store |

The repository has no `lint` script or eslint configuration, so `pnpm architecture:check` is used as its static gate.

Not run: the ST/E2E layer locally (`st.agent-loop-mocked` stalls on `evolve-distribution.test.ts` on this host, untouched by the diff); ST is taken from CI on this pull request. No Windows host was available, so the Windows-only `EACCES` retry is asserted through `transientReplaceCodes("win32")` and injected errnos rather than observed on Windows.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`: 10 files, `+454/−26`. No existing assertion is relaxed.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: writing session run state no longer fails with a bare `EPERM` when another process briefly holds the target file (Windows AV scanners and indexers, SMB/NFS clients), and neither does the deletion journal; a persistent failure now surfaces as a classified `FileReplaceError` that names the destination, the errno and the attempt count instead of a raw `fs` error. A state write that still fails after the retries is logged as `run_scheduler_failed` instead of terminating the API process, and the affected run is recovered as `interrupted` on the next start.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Fixes #860

A compact token count rounds **before** it decides which unit to print, so `999_999` tokens become `${Math.round(999.999)}K` = `1000K` — a number that reads as a million while the exported field still says `999999`. The chart-axis formatter has the same shape (`999_999` → `1000.0K`). One threshold check is off by the unit boundary, not by one token.

## What changed

- `formatCompactTokenValue` crosses into `M` when the thousands rendering would round to `1000` (`Math.round(value / 1_000) >= 1_000`), so `999_500…999_999` print `1.0M` instead of `1000K`. Values that still round below that (`999_499` → `999K`) keep the existing behaviour, as do `10_000` → `10K` and `1_000_000` → `1.0M`.
- `formatChartNumber` applies the same boundary to its one-decimal thousands label (`999.9K` stays `999.9K`, `999_999` becomes `1.0M`, never `1000.0K`), so an axis tick cannot claim a unit the data has not reached.
- `formatTokenField` and every export path are untouched: the exported value is still the exact integer, which is what made the mismatch visible.

868.author: HugoXK
868.body:
Fixes #866

## What this fixes

`sanitizeUploadFilename()` in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` guarded an empty name, a NUL byte, absolute paths, drive letters and traversal, but not Windows reserved device names. On a Windows workspace `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` resolve in every directory and with any extension, so `con.csv`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log` passed the guard and failed later inside the workspace write with a raw `EPERM`/`ENOENT` that the upload response reports as an unclassified error (`CON` targets the console device instead of failing).

The fix rejects them with the same `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` code and error shape the other guard branches use, names the offending file in the message, and strips trailing dots/spaces first because Windows ignores them (`nul.`, `CON .csv`). Legal stems that only begin with a reserved word (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and two-digit ports (`com10.csv`) keep working — the same test asserts both directions.

The guard is platform-independent on purpose, so Linux and macOS reject these names too: portability — an upload must be writable on every supported host, and a file accepted on Linux but unusable on a Windows workspace would only fail later there.

## Red → green

The test was written first and fails on `main` `8708320f`:

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: CON must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

After the fix: `node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 16 / # fail 0`.

Commits keep the pairing: `96b34e1d` test (red), `a2cebfbc` fix.

## Must-fix from review: the refused name now answers 400, not 500

`agent-ci-infra-bot` found the gap: `sanitizeUploadFilename` rejects the new names with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, but the request handler decides 400-vs-500 **by message** (`isKnownClientInputError`, `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32`), and the new message names none of the seven classified patterns. So the exact scenario this PR exists for — uploading `CON.csv` — answered `500 Internal server error` instead of naming the file.

Fixed on the same branch, tip `1a7b1b997bfe5e23af38d3abab59893a33e32ddd`, in two commits:

- `c0173957` (test, red first): a **route-level** test in `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (`WSP-004`) that uploads `CON.csv` through the real HTTP surface and asserts the status, the file name in the body, and that the workspace stayed empty. Before the fix: `500 !== 400`.
- `1a7b1b99` (fix): `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` joins the handler's existing stable-code branches (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`, one line beside `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION`), so the 400 follows the **code** rather than the prose a later wording edit could change. Every branch of the guard is tagged with that code, so this covers the whole family, not just the reserved-name message — no regex added, and no message reworded to please a pattern.

One consideration on where it went: the reviewer's finding points at the message classifier, and adding a ninth prose pattern there would have worked for this message only. The code branch is the smaller and more durable of the two, and it does not loosen any other 400/500 decision.

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` is unchanged and still 16/16 — the function-level contract this PR added is untouched; what changed is the status a client sees.

## Second finding from the same review: the stream syntax (same guard, not a new rule)

The device-name guard took its stem up to the first `.` and never looked at `:`, so `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA` were accepted while `nul.txt` was refused. Windows resolves both to the device in every directory, so that was the same reservation under another spelling:

```
"CON.csv"      -> rejected
"nul.txt"      -> rejected
"NUL. "        -> rejected
"nul:stream"   -> accepted before this commit
"con:$DATA"    -> accepted before this commit
"report:2024.csv" -> accepted before and after
```

Fixed as the **sixth branch of the same predicate**, not as a character rule: `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` now takes its stem before the colon as well as before the dot, and refuses only when that part names a device. A colon in front of an ordinary stem is a legal file name on Linux and macOS, so `report:2024.csv` and `data:2024.tsv` keep passing unchanged — refusing every `:` would have traded this bug for a portability one.

Red first, `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` on `1a7b1b99`:

```
not ok 1 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects the stream syntax of a Windows reserved device name
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   'accepted',
    +   'accepted'
    -   'rejected',
    -   'rejected'
      ]
```

The same test carries the over-rejection guard (`assert.equal(sanitizeUploadFilename("report:2024.csv"), "report:2024.csv")`), which was green before the fix and stays green after it. After: `# tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0` across `workspace-upload.test.ts` and `error-classification.test.ts`.

Nothing outside `sanitizeUploadFilename` had to change for this — the handler branch from the first finding already answers 400 for the code — so this stays one pull request rather than becoming a second one against #866.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**

Fixes #862

## What this fixes

`SessionStore.writeArray()` published state through a `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` file and ran its cleanup in `finally` without a guard:

```ts
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

When `rename` was refused (on Windows an antivirus scanner, search indexer or backup agent holds the freshly written file, so `MoveFileEx` returns `EPERM`) and the `rm` was refused for the same reason, the `finally` threw the bare cleanup `EPERM` and **replaced** the error that explains the loss. The caller then saw an unclassified `EPERM` on a `.tmp` path instead of the classified replace failure, so nothing could tell a locked file apart from a full disk.

The fix swallows the cleanup failure (`.catch(() => undefined)`); the replace error is the one that says what was lost.

## Red → green

| | |
|---|---|
| **Red** `88e6aa07` | `node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → `2 tests / 1 pass / 1 fail`; failing assertion `the cleanup failure must not replace the replace error` (the surfaced error is the mocked `rm` EPERM, the `rename` EPERM is gone) |
| **Green** `0bae8739` | same command → `2 tests / 2 pass / 0 fail` |
| **Review round** `09b4ccb7` | adds the `attempts === 20` / `cause.code` assertions (inert before #857, live after) — same command → `2/2` |

The Security review's anti-forgery assertions are in `09b4ccb7`: when the surfaced error is a `FileReplaceError` (the classified shape #857 introduces on `main`), the test pins `attempts === 20` and `cause.code === "EPERM"`. On this base `writeArray` still calls plain `rename`, so that branch is inert here and becomes live the moment #857 lands — no follow-up tip is needed for it.

The two tests are split (per the Security review): **A** asserts the caller still sees the replace failure when both `rename` and the cleanup `rm` report `EPERM` (it accepts either the raw replace error before #857 or a `FileReplaceError` whose `cause` is it — the check reads `error.cause?.message` too); **B** asserts a failing replace still removes its temporary file, so no `.tmp` is left behind.

Both mocks use `syncBuiltinESMExports()` because `store.ts` imports `rename`/`rm` as named ESM bindings, and both only touch paths whose `basename` starts with `.state-` — the store's own temporary files — so no other write in the fixture is affected. The mock hands control back to the host after the test (`active` flag plus restore) so the next test is not affected by the still-bound ESM export.

Fixes #874

## What this fixes

The API treats `unknown` as a finished-but-unverified outcome for the live surface: `services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:17` and `shell-executions.ts` both define terminal as *not queued and not running*, and an unfinished record found after an API restart is stored as `state: "unknown"` with `finishedAt` set and the reason it stopped being tracked.

But the API deliberately keeps one branch open for it. `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts` `cancel()`:

```ts
// Unknown after restart may still be running remotely; cancellation is safe, resubmission is not.
if (!terminal(execution.state) || execution.state === "unknown") { … }
```

The panel had a single predicate doing both jobs — `const active = (state) => ["queued", "running", "unknown"].includes(state)` (`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:20`) — so an `unknown` record rendered as `process-live` forever (open body, hidden summary, never foldable history), the execution Cancel guard (`:94`) was enabled for it, while the transfer Cancel guard used a hand-written `["queued", "running"]` (`:106`) and disabled its button. The panel gave the same outcome two different answers, and neither the live surface nor the guards matched the API.

Two predicates now:

- `live = state === "queued" || state === "running"` — decides the live surface (`ProcessRecord`) and the **transfer** Cancel guard;
- `cancellable = live(state) || state === "unknown"` — used **only** by the **execution** Cancel guard, because that is exactly the branch the API keeps actionable.

So an unknown execution folds into the ordinary history record (summary row, recorded error shown) yet keeps a reachable "Cancel execution" button; an unknown transfer folds into history with Cancel disabled, because the API settles transfers itself and nothing is left running remotely.

Red first (`4e5369af`, test only), `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/ActivityUnknownOutcome.test.tsx`:

Fixes #877

## What this fixes

Four routes in the same family read one artifact id. `content` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3353`) asks `store.getArtifactVersion()` first and answers 404; `provenance` and `diff` called `artifactVersionProvenance()` / `artifactVersionDiff()`, which throw a bare `new Error("Artifact version not found")` (`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:169` and `:349`). The top-level mapper only turns `Project|Session|Proxy server|Provider|Model not found`, `Execution|Transfer|Timer|Subagent not found: …` and a few codes into 404, so both fell through to the 500 branch — and wrote an `unclassified_request_error` log for what is simply a stale version id.

Now both routes check the version before calling the helper, exactly like `content`, and answer `404 {"error":"Artifact version not found"}`.

The same defect exists one level up, on both versions *list* routes: `/api/projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions` and its Session-scoped sibling pass the id straight to `store.listProjectArtifactVersions()`, which throws a bare `Error("Artifact not found")` — again a 500 plus an `unclassified_request_error`. Both now check the project/Session and the artifact first and answer `404` naming what is missing (`Project not found: …` / `Artifact not found`); the success path is untouched.

`diff` keeps its two comparison-base cases apart, per the issue's expected shape:

- `?against=<id>` given but not found → **404** (a requested resource is missing);
- `?against` absent and the previous version does not exist → **400** `A previous artifact version is unavailable for comparison` (the request asks for a diff this artifact cannot have yet, which is a client-side input problem, not a missing `to` version).

The helpers are unchanged, so their defensive throws still hold for any caller that skips the route.

## Red → green

Red first (`6864420d`, test only), `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts`:

```
content:    { status: 404, error: 'Artifact version not found' }
provenance: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
diff:       { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green after the fixes (`f67b91e9` for the version routes, `3c21ad91` for the list routes): same command → `1/1 pass`; `provenance.test.ts` + `dashboard.test.ts` → `86/86 pass`.

The test drives a real `createApiServer` (`offlineMcpTransport`, no runner) against a freshly created project/session, then asks all three version routes for the same random version id and compares status **and** error body, so a future 500 with a different message cannot pass quietly. It then asks the project-scoped list route for a random artifact id, the Session-scoped one, and a route with a random project id, each expecting 404.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts` → **0** (`1/1`)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` → **0** (`86/86`)
5. `pnpm architecture:check` (no lint script in this repo) → **1**, one failure `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`: sandbox `uv` cannot create a temp file (`Read-only file system (os error 30)`), unrelated to this diff.

Not run: the `?against=` 404 and the missing-previous 400 branches have no version fixture in this harness (creating an artifact version needs an execution), so the test pins the sibling-404 case the issue measured; the two `diff` branches are covered by the code path and stated above. The ST/E2E layer runs in CI.

## Diffstat

```

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: asking for the provenance, the diff, or the version list of an artifact or artifact version that does not exist (an expired link, a version removed by retention, a diff pointing at a deleted version) now answers `404` with the reason instead of `500 Internal server error`; the artifact dialog can say the version is gone instead of failing, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error`.

Fixes #875

## What changed

Both screens now read one decision from a new `apps/web/src/tokenCountFormat.ts`
(`compactTokenParts`): the tier, the rounding and the `".0"` trimming live
there, and each surface only spells the unit it already printed — the usage
page `K`, the model badge `k`. Before this, the badge rounded to whole millions
from 10M (`10_500_000 → "11M"`) while the usage page kept the fraction
(`"10.5M"`) for the same count.

Tiers, now shared:

- 1M and up: one decimal, dropped when it is `".0"` (`1_000_000 → "1M"`,
  `10_500_000 → "10.5M"`, `12_345_678 → "12.3M"`).
- 10K–1M: whole thousands (`200_000 → "200K"` / `"200k"`).
- 1K–10K: one decimal (`6_600 → "6.6K"` / `"6.6k"`).
- Below 1K: the plain count.
- The rounding decides the crossing: `999_999 → "1M"`, never `"1000K"`.

Measured before the change on base `89cd2d30` (badge / usage page):

```text
    999999  badge  1000k   usage 1000K
   1000000  badge     1M   usage 1.0M
   1500000  badge     2M   usage 1.5M
   9960000  badge    10M   usage 10.0M
  10500000  badge    11M   usage 10.5M
  12345678  badge    12M   usage 12.3M
```

Below one million the number is shared and only the unit glyph still differs,
as it already did on both screens; the test pins that difference (`"200k"` vs
`"200K"`) so a later "one spelling" refactor is a conscious change. Two readouts
move as a consequence of one rule: the badge prints one decimal in the 1K–10K
tier (`2_000 → "2.0k"`, no test pinned the old `"2k"`) and a whole million loses
`".0"` (`1_000_000 → "1M"` on the usage page, which is also the direction of
#864).

The shared ladder carries the `999_999 → "1M"` crossing that #864 adds to the
usage formatter as well; whichever of that pull request and this one merges
second resolves the overlap mechanically, the numbers stay the same.

formatter's `1.0M` → `1M`) → #869 (the badge's `1_500_000` `2M` → `1.5M`) →
