886.body:
Fixes #883

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`_NODE_LIMIT` is a hard cap of 500 nodes, and the contract at `query.py:319` says only results **beyond** it carry `truncated: True`. The flag was computed *after* a Cypher `LIMIT` bound to exactly the cap, so the Python side could never observe a 501st row: a complete 500-row answer and a cut one were indistinguishable and both reported `truncated: true`. The panel then drew `N of 500+ (truncated) match(es) in view` — the `+` asserting a further match that does not exist — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes was badged as partial.

`query.py` now has one helper, `_cap_page(rows)`, returning the kept page and `len(rows) > _NODE_LIMIT` as the flag. Two shapes use it:

- **Cypher-driven reads** — `query_match` (`:431`), `by_node_type` (`:465`), `by_edge_type` (`:518`), `get_subgraph` (`:272`) and `_serialize_subgraph` (`:1298`): the Cypher limit is bound to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, the page is cut to `_NODE_LIMIT` and the extra row alone decides the flag. `query_match`/`by_node_type` count the **raw rows** before `_to_hit`, the variant the issue prefers: a row dropped because its label has no id field is not a truncation. In `get_subgraph` the node-id set used to filter edges and synthesize the folded scope→product surrogates is built from the kept page, so no rendered edge points at a node the caller did not receive.
- **Assembled reads** — `get_scope_expansion` (`:898`) and `get_group_expansion` (`:1024`): these build their node set from several queries (children + produces subtree + edge endpoints; group members + one surrogate edge each) and have **no Cypher `LIMIT`** to raise, so `cap + 1` does not apply to them. The cap is applied to the assembled page instead, and an edge whose endpoint fell outside the page is dropped rather than rendered against an absent node. `get_group_expansion` and `_serialize_subgraph` were not in the issue's list of five: they carry the identical predicate (`len(...) >= _NODE_LIMIT` over a set that had not been cut at all — flagging a page they never truncated), so they are fixed in the same slice rather than left as the same defect on two more surfaces.

`total` keeps its previous meaning (the number of rows the response carries), so no client contract changes; `services/api` and the web panel forward the flag verbatim and need no edit.

## Red first

Test commit `9ce6d309` (test only), base `89cd2d30`:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q
14 failed in 0.50s
```

Three distinct failure shapes prove the tests reach the real paths:

- `assert True is False` — a complete 500-row answer reported as truncated (the reported defect, once per capped reader);
- `assert 500 == (500 + 1)` — the reader bound `$limit` to the cap itself, so the flag cannot be decided at all;
- `assert 501 == 500` — the two assembled readers returned all 501 nodes: the page had not been cut even though it was flagged.

Green at `e1957043`: the same command gives `14 passed in 0.15s`.

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto the current main tip `89cd2d30` (it was first based on a mirror that still served `8708320f`); `services/memory-graph` has no upstream drift between the two, and every reading below was taken again at the rebased commits.

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` (7 readers × exactly-500 / 501) |
| memory-graph suite, tip | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `123 passed, 15 warnings, 78 errors` |
| memory-graph suite, same tree without the new file (baseline) | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `109 passed, 14 warnings, 78 errors` |
| error set | `diff` of the `ERROR tests/...` lines of the two runs | identical (78 lines) |

The 78 errors are the pre-existing `@needs_neo4j` suite on this host — every one fails in setup with `Failed: needs a live Neo4j`, and the set is node-for-node the same with and without this diff (`187` collected before, `201` after the 14 new cases).

The cases assert more than the flag: for each reader a 501-row result must return exactly 500 rows; the assembled readers must drop the spine edge that points into the cut row; `_serialize_subgraph` and the four Cypher readers must bind `$limit` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`.

Not run: anything needing a live Neo4j (the Cypher and the rendered panel text itself), because there is no graph on this host and `ci.yml` has no memory-graph job — the issue notes this, so the local pytest output above is the acceptance evidence. The TypeScript gates (`pnpm --recursive typecheck`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`) are not run: the diff touches no TypeScript.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…e1dee252`: 3 files, `+656/−19` (`query.py` `+93/−19`, `tests/test_node_limit.py` `+320`, `tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` `+243`). No existing assertion is relaxed.

## Review fix (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` on `e1957043`, review `5773456818`)

`yuanzhou75` found that the new test file stopped the whole `UT` layer before a single case ran: the tagged audit (`test/support/tagged/python/science_tags.py:103-108`) accepts only `pytest.mark.parametrize` arguments that pass `ast.literal_eval`, and `CAP` / `CAP + 1` are a `Name` and a `BinOp`. Because the audit runs in `pytest_collect_file`, collection aborted with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: .../test_node_limit.py:107` and `merge-gate` never evaluated. Fixed at `04ce9c89`, in the shape the review asked for:

- **All seven** parameter tables (lines 105/123/155/181/227/266/290) are now `[(500, False), (501, True)]` with their existing ids, and each case opens with `assert query._NODE_LIMIT == 500  # the table above is literal on purpose`. `CAP` stays and is still used by the body assertions, including the one requiring `$limit == CAP + 1`.
- One more registration defect the audit then exposed: the module carried **no** `science_tags` module mark, so once the audit passed the catalog step raised `ValueError: Missing tag group: category` — the same `PYTHON_COLLECTION_FAILED` for the layer, one step later. It now has the line every sibling in this suite has: `pytestmark = pytest.mark.science_tags(category='ut', os='linux', arch=('amd64', 'arm64'))`.

Verified at `04ce9c89` with the harness's own code, not a stand-in for it:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && python3 -c "import sys; sys.path[:0]=['../../test/support/tagged/python']; import science_tags, pathlib; science_tags.audit_source(pathlib.Path('tests/test_node_limit.py'))"
(no output) exit 0        # before: ValueError: DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: tests/test_node_limit.py:107
```

```
$ PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=<repo>/test/support/tagged/python \
  uv run --project services/memory-graph --extra test python -m pytest -p science_tags \
  --strict-markers --rootdir <repo> --collect-only -q \
  --science-root=<repo> --science-catalog=<file> $(ls services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py)
201 tests collected in 0.99s     # exit 0
```

That is the command `coordinator.mjs`'s `collect()` runs — same `-p science_tags`, `--strict-markers`, `--rootdir`, `--science-catalog`, plugin autoload off — over every source `pythonSources('memory-graph')` globs. The catalog it wrote has 201 entries, 14 of them from this file, tagged `category:ut, os:linux, arch:amd64, arch:arm64, tier:l2, status:reviewed, ...`. Before the change the same command died at `:107`; with only the tables fixed it died again at the missing `category`.

| gate | command | reading at `04ce9c89` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tag audit | `science_tags.audit_source(tests/test_node_limit.py)` | exit 0 |
| tagged collection, whole project | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `201 tests collected`, exit 0, 201 catalog entries |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed, 1 warning` |
| memory-graph suite | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` |

The one warning the module adds is `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.science_tags`, which every sibling module in this suite emits when pytest runs without the tagged plugin (`tests/test_logging_config.py` on its own gives `1 passed, 1 warning`); the plugin registers the marker and the collection above passes `--strict-markers`. The 78 errors are the unchanged `@needs_neo4j` setup failures.

No other file changed; the five commits stay separate: `9ce6d309` red test, `e1957043` fix, `04ce9c89` this registration fix, `86bbd1a5` the rule cases below, `e1dee252` the rule fix.

### Second review: one meaning for `truncated` (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6zusPi`)

The review found three counting conventions for one flag in the same PR. I took the first of its two options and made it the only one: **`truncated` means the backend returned more rows than `_NODE_LIMIT`, counted on the rows that were read and *before* a row is dropped for having no identity.**

Why this rule and not "count only renderable hits":

- **Only the returned-row count can be decided.** Each Cypher read binds `LIMIT` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, and that one extra row is the whole probe. Filtering first spends the probe on a row that cannot be rendered: 500 readable hits plus an unrenderable 501st would look *complete* although a renderable 502nd may exist, which is a completeness claim nothing checked. The returned-row count claims only what the extra row proves — the answer went past the cap.
- **It is the question the panel text asks.** `N of 500+ (truncated)` says the graph holds more matches than are shown. True when 501 rows came back even if one cannot be drawn; false when 501 came back and the response says "complete".
- **A short page stays complete.** 500 rows with one unrenderable row → 499 rendered, `truncated: false`: nothing was left unread, so there is nothing to disclose. Both directions are pinned below.

What changed:

- `get_subgraph` now caps the returned `(label, node)` rows and then runs `_node_identity`; `_serialize_subgraph` caps the returned rows and then runs `_to_hit`. Those are the two readers that capped the *filtered* list.
- `query_match`, `by_node_type`, `by_edge_type` already capped the returned rows; `query_match`'s comment argued the opposite and now states the rule, and the other two carry the same sentence.
- `get_scope_expansion` and `get_group_expansion` cap the assembled page, where every element already has an identity by construction, so "rows read" and "renderable rows" coincide there — no behaviour change, and the comment says so.
- `_cap_page`'s docstring states the rule once, and why the filter has to run after the cut. The review's nit (`nodes = list(hit_rows)` and a rebind on the next line) disappears with the restructure: `nodes` is built directly from the kept rows.

`tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` (new, 6 cases) pins the rule rather than the arithmetic: an unrenderable row as the 501st sets the flag on `query_match`, `by_edge_type`, `get_subgraph` and `_serialize_subgraph`, and a complete 500-row page that holds one unrenderable row stays complete on `query_match` and `get_subgraph`. Two of the six fail on `86bbd1a5` — `assert False is True` on the two readers that filtered first — and pass on `e1dee252`; the four that already held are there so a future reader cannot silently move one side into the other's shape again.

Deferred, deliberately not in this PR: `get_scope_expansion` / `get_group_expansion` still read every child/member and cut in Python, so the cap bounds the response and not the query work — same as before this PR, noted for follow-up.

Readings at `e1dee252`:

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rule cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit_rule.py -q` | `6 passed` |
| cap cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` |
| whole suite | `pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` (the 78 unchanged) |
| tag audit, both files | `science_tags.audit_source(...)` | exit 0 each |
| tagged collection | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `207 tests collected`, exit 0, 207 catalog entries |

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: a memory-graph search that matches exactly 500 nodes no longer says `500+ (truncated)` — it reports the count as complete — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes is no longer badged as partial. A query that really has more than the cap still reports `truncated` and still returns 500 rows.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Fixes #885

## What this fixes

In an `zh-CN` session a tool card mixed two languages inside one frame: `输入` came from the message catalog, and the headings immediately below it — `Result`, `Error`, `Created files`, `Produced artifacts` — were English literals minted by the parser. The copy button inherited the English half, so its accessible label read `复制Result`.

The parser keeps its English labels on purpose: `parseToolResultSections` output is read by the existing parser test and is the value the per-section copy button copies, so translating there would change a contract to fix a rendering defect. The locale is applied where the card renders instead, in `apps/web/src/timeline/ToolIoSections.tsx`:

- `Result` / `Error` reuse `timeline.result` / `timeline.error`, the two keys that already existed in the catalog and had no caller — the wiring was simply never finished.
- `Created files` / `Produced artifacts` get `timeline.createdFiles` / `timeline.producedArtifacts`, added in both `en` and `zh-CN`.
- `stdout` / `stderr` are left verbatim in every locale: they are protocol stream names, not prose.

## Red first

`apps/web/tests/tool-result-labels.test.tsx` on base `89cd2d30`, before the fix:

```
$ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/tool-result-labels.test.tsx
not ok 1 - USG-021 tool result headings follow the reader's locale
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
        '输入',
    +   'Result'
    -   '结果'
      ]
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The first heading in that diff is already `输入`, so the failure is the untranslated headings and nothing about the harness. The test covers all four headings, both locales, the failed-run case, the copy labels (`复制结果` / `复制错误`, and no `复制Result`), and the two verbatim stream names.

## After

```
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

## Gates, all on the pushed tip `d4c482be637952fd1c05b67d3acd0890ea208e27`

Ran:

- `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → exit 0
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` → `# tests 1216 / # pass 1216 / # fail 0`, exit 0 (new test is `ok 1181 - USG-021`; the existing `tool-result-sections.test.tsx` parser contract is unchanged and still green)
- `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1` → `{"status":"PASS","planned":4,"executed":4,"passed":4,"failed":0,"skipped":0}`, exit 0

Not run: the L2/ST profiles beyond L1 locally (the change is a rendered string, no flow), and CodeCheck on the GitCode mirror, which runs upstream.

## Diff, base `89cd2d30`

```text
 apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts              |  4 +++
 apps/web/src/timeline/ToolIoSections.tsx   | 26 ++++++++++++++++++++--
 apps/web/tests/tool-result-labels.test.tsx | 70 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 3 files changed, 97 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

Commits keep the red/green pairing: `6c7d12c5` test (red), `d4c482be` fix.

Release category: release:fix
User impact: in `zh-CN` the tool card's section headings and its copy labels are Chinese (`结果` / `错误` / `创建的文件` / `生成的文件`, `复制结果`), matching `输入` above them; the English UI is unchanged and `stdout`/`stderr` stay verbatim in both.
Compatibility and migration: none — the parser's labels and the copy payload are untouched.

890.author: HugoXK
890.body:
Fixes #887

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`POST /api/sessions/:id/files` resolved `body.path` through `resolveWorkspaceFile` — which only refuses absolute paths and escapes — and wrote the result straight to disk. On a Windows workspace that makes `CON` target the console device and `nul.txt` fail with a raw `EPERM` the handler never classifies, so the client saw `500 Internal server error`. The reserved-device-name guard existed only in the upload path.

Chosen fix: **direction 2** — the predicate became a workspace invariant instead of an upload-only check.

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — new exported `isWindowsReservedDeviceName(name)`, sitting directly beside `assertWorkspacePath`. It matches the stems Windows resolves in every directory (`con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`, `conin$`, `conout$`), strips trailing dots/spaces first (`nul.`, `CON `), and treats everything before the first dot as the stem, because the extension is irrelevant to a device. It is exported through the package index (`export * from "./workspace.js"`).
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — the write route walks **every segment** of `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` (the helper is a segment rule, so `CON/notes.txt` is refused before `mkdir("…/CON")`) and answers **400 naming the offending segment**. The route keeps accepting nested relative paths; the upload path's "plain basename only" rule is still not imposed here.

Why not direction 1 (call `sanitizeUploadFilename` in the handler): on this base that function has **no** reserved-name branch — it only rejects empty/NUL/absolute/traversal names, which `resolveWorkspaceFile` already enforces — so calling it today would be a no-op for the reported defect. Adding the rule inside it here would duplicate `#868`'s open hunk in the same function (and that PR exists to fix exactly that statement). Putting the predicate beside `assertWorkspacePath` gives both write paths one home once they meet.

### Relation to `#868` (open)

`#868` carries the identical rule inline in `sanitizeUploadFilename`. This diff deliberately does **not** touch `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`, so the two do not overlap: when `#868` lands, its guard should call `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` and drop the inline copy (one hunk), leaving main with a single implementation. Whichever merges second does that; if `#868` lands first I will rebase this branch and make that change here.

## Review fix — P2, a device name in a directory segment (review `5773758545`, reviewed at `93af68c8`)

The first version applied the predicate to `basename(target)`, i.e. only the last segment. The route accepts nested relative paths, so `body.path = "CON/notes.txt"` had basename `notes.txt` and passed the guard; the write then reached `mkdir(dirname(target), { recursive: true })`. On a Windows host `CreateDirectory("…/CON")` fails (Node surfaces `EPERM`/`ENOENT`), which is the same unclassified 500 this PR removes; on Linux it creates an unportable `CON/` directory. The helper was already documented as a segment rule, so the call site was the narrow part.

Fixed as asked: the route now splits `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` on the host separator and refuses the first reserved segment. That subsumes the old last-segment case, and the message names the segment the client must change (`"CON"` for `CON/notes.txt`, `"nul.dir"` for `nul.dir/x.csv`) instead of a basename it never sent.

The predicate's doc comment no longer claims to be called from every writer. It states the per-segment rule, names where it is applied today (this route), and says that the agent-side workspace tools, which write through `assertWorkspacePath`, are not wired to it yet.

`WSP-005` (`services/api/src/server.test.ts`) now covers, in addition to the four top-level names and the four look-alikes from the first version:

- `CON/notes.txt` → 400, the message names `CON`
- `nul.dir/x.csv` → 400, the message names `nul.dir` (stem before the first dot is `nul`, and Windows refuses the directory too)
- `notes/CON.txt` → 400 (control: clean directory, device-name file — refused before this change too)
- `conifer/notes.txt` → 201 (control: the walk must not start refusing legitimate nested paths)

## Red first

Original case at base `89cd2d30` (test commit `1c3259df`, now the first half of `WSP-005`):

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: CON must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The two new directory cases are red at the previous tip `93af68c8` (`0a1ca4fc` is test only). The loop stops at the first failure, so each was run as the only new case:

```
$ node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
  error: CON/notes.txt must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
$ (same command, `nul.dir/x.csv` as the only new case)
  error: nul.dir/x.csv must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
```

`notes/CON.txt` and `conifer/notes.txt` are green at `93af68c8` by design: they are the controls, so they carry no red reading.

## Validation

The API tests load `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from its built `dist`, so the package is built first (CI does the same: the shared runner runs `pnpm build` before the heavy layers).

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| workspace build | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/workspace build` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (api) | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (workspace) | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/workspace typecheck` | exit 0 |
| tests typecheck | `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | exit 0 |
| route case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts` | `1/1` pass (`services/api`) |
| workspace route group | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "WSP-00" src/server.test.ts` | `3/3` pass |
| package UT | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/workspace test` | `100 tests / 100 pass / 0 fail` |
| api UT | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` | `1866 tests / 1860 pass / 6 fail`: 5 environment (`No module named uvicorn` in `services/evolve/.venv`; `No module named 'reportlab'` ×3; missing `@openai/codex-linux-x64`), 1 load flake in `evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` (`timed out waiting for the run to finish`) that passes on its own (`--test-name-pattern "settled"` → `3/3`). None touch this diff. |

Not run: a real Windows host — the guard is deliberately platform-independent, so the Linux route test exercises the same code path; there is no Windows-only branch in it.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`: 3 files, `+112/−5` (`workspace.ts` `+27`, `http/index.ts` `+17/−5`, `server.test.ts` `+68`). No existing assertion is relaxed; the only edit to an existing test line is the look-alike loop gaining `conifer/notes.txt`.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: writing a session file whose name or directory component is a Windows device (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, `CON/notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv`) now answers 400 naming the offending segment, on every platform, instead of returning 201 and creating a file a Windows host cannot open (or a write that silently goes to the console or fails as a 500). Ordinary names such as `conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `com10.csv` and `conifer/notes.txt` are unaffected.
Compatibility and migration: none — only names Windows itself cannot create are refused.

Fixes #889 ## What the user sees A background execution that ended because it was cancelled is summarised as an unknown outcome: the runtime notice card prints `Synced 1 background execution result(s)` with `1 unconfirmed` above a record whose own badge reads `cancelled`. The card contradicts itself about the same execution, and it tells the researcher the result is unknown when they cancelled it themselves. ## Red first `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` gains one case: a notice with a single `state: "cancelled"` execution record must print `1 cancelled`, keep the record's `activity-badge cancelled`, and must not print `unconfirmed`. On base `0eb12a0a`, before any source change, that case fails: ``` not ok 4 - a cancelled execution is summarised as cancelled, not unconfirmed error: |- The input did not match the regular expression /1 cancelled/. Input: '

Synced 1 background execution result(s) 1 unconfirmed

...' # tests 4 # pass 3 # fail 1 ``` The other three cases in the file pass, so the failure is the new bucket, not the file. ## The fix `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx` gives `cancelled` its own bucket instead of folding every non-completed, non-failed state into `chat.wakeNoticeUnconfirmed`. The catalog gains `chat.wakeNoticeCancelled` (`{count} cancelled` / `{count} 项已取消`); the record badge at `:26` already maps `cancelled` correctly and is left alone. `queued`, `running` and `unknown` stay in the unconfirmed bucket — a still-open execution is what the word means — and a second case pins that: `1 completed · 1 cancelled · 2 unconfirmed` for a notice with one record in each of those states. The card is display-only: no notice data, dispatch or API shape changes. ## Ran ``` cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx -> 5 tests / 5 pass / 0 fail (4/5 before the fix commit; case 4 red as quoted above) pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web typecheck -> clean (tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit) pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test -> 1221 tests / 1221 pass / 0 fail CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1 -> PASS, planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4 ``` Tagged collector, so this is not a `#882`-style green that never ran. The node half of the `ut` slice selects `apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx` (`nodeSources` glob, then the `category:ut` filter that `shared.mjs` applies: 554 of 566 declared node sources), and the same collector, plan builder and worker ran its five cases: ``` node .local/889-plan.mjs node sources: 566; ut node sources: 554; target in ut set: true cases collected from apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx: 5 (all five ids listed) node test/support/tagged/cli.mjs run --plan .local/889-plan-node/plan.json --import tsx {"status":"PASS","planned":5,"passed":5,"skipped":0} ``` `cli.mjs --path` refuses `.tsx` sources by design (`Unsupported test source`), which is why the run above goes through a plan built from the same collector instead of `--path`; the `ut` slice itself reaches this file through the `apps/web/tests/**/*.test.*` glob. ## Not run No browser or E2E journey: the change is one bucketing expression in a display component, and the L1 slice above covers the layer that renders it. `ci:ut` end-to-end was not run on this workstation because the Python project venvs are absent; the Node half is covered by the plan run quoted above. ## Diffstat `git diff --stat 0eb12a0a…HEAD` (base `main` `0eb12a0a`): ``` apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx | 9 ++++++++- apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts | 2 ++ apps/web/tests/WakeNotice.test.tsx | 15 +++++++++++++++ 3 files changed, 25 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) ``` ## Release Release category: release:fix User impact: a cancelled background execution is summarised as `1 cancelled` instead of `1 unconfirmed`, matching the `cancelled` badge on the record below it; open executions still read `unconfirmed`. Compatibility and migration: none — display-only change, no notice data or API shape changes.
